claim.claim: Amazon's operating income in the quarter ended March 31, 2026 benefited from one-time items that overstate its underlying profitability.

verdict.label: CONTRADICTED

contradicting_evidence.quote: Other operating expense (income), net was $308 million and $447 million for Q1 2025 and Q1 2026, and was primarily related to charges associated with damaged data centers in the Middle East in Q1 2026, asset impairments, and the amortization of intangible assets.

verdict.reasoning_summary:
The claim asserts that Amazon's operating income in Q1 2026 benefited from one-time items that overstate its underlying profitability. This is a qualitative/interpretive claim about whether one-time items inflated operating income.

The evidence contradicts this claim. E1 shows that "Other operating expense (income), net" was $447 million in Q1 2026, primarily related to charges for damaged data centers in the Middle East, asset impairments, and amortization. These are expenses (not income), and they reduced operating income rather than inflating it. The damaged data center charges appear to be one-time items, but they had a negative impact on operating income.

While E4 mentions net gains of $15.6 billion from Anthropic investments in Q1 2026, these gains flow through "Other comprehensive income" (as stated in E4's context about reclassification adjustments), not operating income. Operating income is calculated before these investment gains.

Therefore, the one-time items identified in the filing (damaged data center charges) actually understated rather than overstated operating income in Q1 2026, directly contradicting the claim.
